My husband and I had a terrible argument that morning.

It was one of those arguments where love suddenly feels like hatred, and the person who knows all your weaknesses uses them against you.

"You will regret the way you treat me," he said, grabbing his car keys.

"And you will regret ever marrying me!" I shouted back.

He stared at me for a moment. I expected him to say something, but he simply walked away and slammed the door.

That was the last time I heard my husband's voice.

note_tweet.text:
So - after all the crazy conspiracies and the false 'blame the (non-existent) carer' crackpottery - it transpires the unfortunate who chose to provoke Altai the tiger to maul him to death at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park by invading his enclosure had been a child actor and liked posing with crossbows and bibles. He had ironically appeared in an ITV series titled May Contain Nuts and a BBC programme, True Stories.

'Vulnerable' and 'on strong medication' William Chapman was able to get himself to the park, buy a ticket, pose for and upload photographs and videos. He also conducted a (recorded) conversation quite rationally with a lady before leaping to his ultimate demise.

The 'blame the tiger' narrative to this sad saga must now end. This unfortunate incident teaches several lessons, but the key ones are these - Don't mess with wildlife and don't believe the crazy claptrap that spreads on social media like wildfire; it never ends well.

I do hope the family of William Chapman are now able to appropriately grieve and find closure and I do hope Altai the tiger can now be again appreciated and respectfully observed from a distance as he truly deserves.

#WilliamChapman #Altai #Tiger #YorkshireWildlifePark #ITV #BBC #MayContainNuts #TrueStories #TeamTiger

Last spring I applied for a job as a joke.

It was a late Tuesday night and I'd had two glasses of wine. The company was a design firm, the listing demanded "ten years of experience in a field that does not yet exist," and I thought, Someone should respond to this honestly.

My cover letter said, "I am excellent at nothing in particular, but I am very cheerful. I once talked a man out of a parking ticket by describing my cat. I make tea for people without being asked. I will not be good at your job, but I'll be fun to sit next to."

I attached a CV that listed "Survived" under every previous role. I hit send and went to bed laughing.

Three days later I got an email: "We'd love to meet you. Can you come in on Thursday at 2pm?"...
